page: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the QEMU hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 125.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is supported by a 600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific areas, particularly in memory and single-core operations. The instance achieves a top-tier rating in the Passmark memory score and high-speed text generation for small language models. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are also strong, placing in the top 25%. Most other compute metrics, including multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench suites, and Redis SET operations, perform within the average range for this hardware class.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx53 offers dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring predictable performance without resource contention from neighboring instances. The lack of bundled public IPv4 addresses and GPU accelerators represents a tradeoff for network-heavy or deep learning workloads. This profile is highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded data processing, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring consistent CPU and memory performance.
